title: Acute pulmonary edema in a COPD patient
objectives: Differentiate CHF from COPD ("cardiac wheeze", JVD, edema, capno shape)
CPAP early (SpO2 <94, RR >25, accessory use; SBP >= 100)
IV + Med Direction for SL nitro dosed by SBP
Don't withhold O2 from hypoxic COPD pt; watch for fatigue
resources: CPAP, O2 (full tanks), DuoNeb, IV, NTG SL, 12-lead, BVM. UVMMC ~6 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 41 Pleasant St, Apt 3, for a 78-year-old male, difficulty breathing. Caller is his wife. Time out 0215.

scene.location: 2nd floor apartment, bedroom. Narrow stairs, no elevator.
scene.setup: Pt tripoding on bed edge, home NC 2 L, pillows stacked, nebulizer on nightstand (just used).
scene.moulage: Pale/dusky lips, misted sweat, swollen ankles (padding under socks).
scene.roles: Pt actor; wife ("it's his COPD, the neb didn't work").

patient.name: Walter Hebert
patient.cc: Can't breathe x 2 hr, woke him from sleep
patient.on_arrival: Tripod, 1-2 word answers, frothy cough, sweaty, panicked. Wheezing audible from door.

SAMPLE: SOB, can't lie flat, cough w/ pink froth, ankles swollen x1 wk
Tiotropium, albuterol neb, home O2 2 L, **furosemide (ran out 5 days ago)**, metoprolol, lisinopril
Woke at 0000 gasping; neb x2 at home, no relief
OPQRST: Worse lying flat; neb didn't help
Worse over 2 hr. 3 pillows x1 wk

primary: RR 34, accessory muscles, retractions. **Wheeze + crackles to mid-fields**
Radial strong, rapid. Skin cool, diaphoretic, dusky
**HIGH**: acute pulmonary edema (CHF) - not just COPD

vitals.other: Crackles + wheeze, JVD, edema. Sinus tach
No better, more anxious, crackles higher
Less work of breathing, 3-4 word sentences

vitals.trigger: 5 min after MD-ordered NTG 0.8 mg SL
vitals.other: Crackles bases only. Talking full sentences
Head bobbing, sleepy -> BVM w/ PEEP, d/c CPAP

flow.give: Wife: "It's his COPD, the neb isn't working." Stage **A**.
Give lung sounds, JVD, edema, capno card when found. Wife: "He ran out of his water pill."

branches.if: Treated as COPD only (nebs, O2 limited)

expected: CHF recognized: crackles, JVD, edema, orthopnea

flow.give: Pt pulls at mask: "I can't, I'm suffocating!"

branches.then: SpO2 84%; expect remove CPAP (5.4), suction, NRB/BVM, re-apply only when airway clear

flow.give: MD (if contacted, SBP 160-200): "NTG 0.8 mg SL, may repeat q5 until SBP 140."

branches.if: NTG given w/o MD or before IV

expected: PDE-5 use asked; SBP rechecked q5

flow.give: Stage **D**. Narrow stairs. Pt can't lie flat.
expected: Portable O2 supply checked (CPAP uses lots)

branches.if: Portable O2 reads 500 psi at top of stairs
branches.then: expect tank swap/plan before moving; CPAP uses high flow

flow.give: Evaluator plays ED: "Prep for CPAP patient?"
expected: ED notified: CPAP pt, NTG doses

critical: No CPAP in pt meeting criteria (SpO2 <94, RR >25, accessory use)
CPAP applied with SBP < 100 or decreased LOC/no airway control
Nitroglycerin by AEMT without Med Direction order (3.3A)
O2 withheld from hypoxic pt due to COPD history
Failure to recognize fatigue/hypercapnia and assist ventilation
differentials: Orthopnea, pink froth, crackles, JVD, edema, HTN, ran out of diuretic
Square capno, crackles, JVD, edema, no relief from nebs
Crackles, JVD w/ HTN, edema bilateral
debrief: What told you this was CHF and not COPD?
How does the capnography waveform help sort them?
Why does CPAP help pulmonary edema?
What is an AEMT's route to nitro in 3.3A vs 3.0A?
Signs CPAP is failing and what you do next

crew_card.dispatch: 41 Pleasant St, Apt 3 (2nd floor). 78 y/o M, difficulty breathing. Caller: wife.
crew_card.on_arrival: Older man sitting on edge of bed, leaning forward, gasping, on nasal cannula. Oxygen machine humming. Wife in doorway.

actor_card.Act: Tripod, gasp, 1-2 words, cough into tissue. Refuse to lie back.
actor_card.On CPAP: Panic for ~30 s, pull at mask. Calm down if crew coaches you. Then speak in longer phrases.
actor_card.If asked about meds: "Ran out of the water pill last week." No Viagra/Cialis.
actor_card.If no CPAP by T+15: Get sleepy, slow breathing, head drops, mumble.
actor_card.Wife: Insist "it's his COPD" until crew explains.

show_cards.title: 12-LEAD
show_cards.caption: Computer interpretation: Sinus tachycardia 118. Left ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization abnormality. No acute MI criteria. Simulated - not to scale.

show_cards.title: CAPNOGRAPHY
show_cards.caption: EtCO2 34   RR 34
show_cards.cue: Square waveform (no bronchospasm) - supports CHF over COPD

show_cards.title: LUNG SOUNDS
show_cards.body:
Crackles bases to mid-fields bilaterally.
Expiratory wheeze throughout.

show_cards.title: NECK / LEGS
show_cards.body:
JVD sitting upright.
2+ pitting edema both shins.

show_cards.title: NIGHTSTAND
show_cards.body:
Albuterol nebs (2 used tonight)
Tiotropium
Furosemide 40 mg - **EMPTY**, filled 6 wk ago
Metoprolol, lisinopril

moulage_tags.text: Neck veins distended while sitting upright
Crackles bases to mid-fields; wheezes throughout

learn_more.topic: acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema in a patient with COPD
learn_more.focus: telling CHF from COPD in the field (lung sounds, JVD, capnography waveform), CPAP evidence, and high-dose nitroglycerin
